newsitem.title: INDIA: India to decide hike in govt salaries "shortly".
newsitem.headline: India to decide hike in govt salaries "shortly".

text.p: The Indian cabinet will soon decide the implementation of a panel's report recommending a hike in salaries of government employees, a government statement said on Tuesday.

"Various issues relating to the implementation including the representation received from the employees' organisations were discussed (by the Indian cabinet)", the statement said. "A final view on the subject will be taken shortly."

Earlier on Tuesday, Finance Minister P.Chidambaram said that there was no change in a decision to hike the salaries of government employees, and denied an official's statement that the hikes were withheld.

The high-powered pay panel had submitted its report in January, and the cabinet approved last month a 135-billion- rupee spending plan to effect its recommendations. Around 5.2 million employees stand to gain from the pay hikes.
Opposition members wanted the government explain its position after a senior official was quoted as saying that the planned pay hikes which were to take effect from August one had been withheld.

Cabinet Secretary T.S.R. Subramaniam, India's most senior civil servant, told television reporters on Monday the government had withheld the pay hikes because agitating employees were dissatisfied despite the government's best efforts to increase their salaries.

Government employee unions protested against the government's decision saying junior employees were unhappy over the pay hikes given to them. They said the new pay packets would widen the gap between highest and lowest employees.
There were also protests over the planned abolition of 350,000 government jobs considered redundant.
Chidambaram said the government notifications to effect the pay hikes approved by the cabinet were being held back as some procedural clarifications were needed.

"No particular day had been decided upon for issuing the notification by the various ministries. One or two issues need to be clarified. Therefore the notification is being held back by a few days," Chidambaram said.
Chidambaran said that the implmentation of the Pay Commission recommendations would take effect from the first of July irrespective of when the orders are actually issued.
